doctrine: Photography is a business tool, not art. Revenue thesis: specialize in one niche, price on business outcomes (not hours), systematize delivery, layer passive income on active service income. Active revenue (events $200-1k, product $50-200/image, headshots $150-700, real estate $100-400/property, weddings $1500-7500, B2B retainer $500-3000/mo). Passive: white-label print automation at 3-5x cost, commercial licensing annual renewals, digital products (presets/templates), affiliate revenue, gear rental. Acquisition: spec work (shoot product, watermark, pitch to brand), value-first outreach (identify visual gaps, free trial, convert to retainer), physical partnerships (matted prints with QR codes in high-traffic spots). Pricing: 3-tier anchor model (Entry/Value/HomeRun), use round numbers, remove commas ($2160 not $2,160), price on outcomes not time, separate wage system (fixed weekly salary + business profit). KPIs: CLV (lifetime value per client), CPA (marketing cost per booking <15-20%), CR (inquiry-to-booking conversion). Scaling paths: (A) premium positioning (maximize margin, raise prices 20-50%), (B) team expansion (document SOPs, hire associates at day rate $300-500, you handle creative direction). Authority pivot (teach/courses/workshops, highest leverage $10k to $30k/mo). Operator playbook: Phase 1 (days 1-60, test 4 niches 3 projects each), Phase 2 (months 2-4, niche portfolio + spec work + 5 paying clients), Phase 3 (months 4-8, gallery upsells + digital product + print store + licensing), Phase 4 (months 8-12, consistent revenue + hire/raise prices), Phase 5 (year 2+, educational products + B2B retainers + transition to operator). Core principle: talent is table stakes, systems are the moat.

workflows: Pebble-to-Boulder Revenue Sequence: active service -> gallery upsell -> digital product -> print store -> licensing -> affiliate -> teaching
Spec Work Method: buy brand product, shoot 10-20 images, watermark, pitch to marketing manager, convert to retainer
Value-First Outreach: identify visual gap, name it in pitch, free/low-cost trial, prove competence, convert to contract
3-Tier Pricing Anchor: design Tier 1 (entry, quick turnaround), Tier 2 (ideal sale, best margin), Tier 3 (home run, makes Tier 2 reasonable)
Team Expansion: document SOP, recruit shooters at day rate, charge client full rate, keep margin
Authority Pivot: client work proves system, teaching proves articulation, both reinforce each other (3-leg model)

operating_rules: Camera is a business tool, not an art project. Compete on ROI delivered, not aesthetics.
Spec work beats portfolios. One real brand shoot worth 100 generic portfolio images.
Price on business outcomes (listing-speed, team credibility, website refresh), never hourly rates.
Gallery upsell: shoot 25, deliver 5 contracted, sell 20 remaining at $40 each via gallery. 48-hour expiration drives urgency.
Licensing is real passive income. Add renewal clauses to every commercial contract. One shoot, years of income.
Print margins: white-label fulfillment, never touch physical product. 3-5x markup at marginal cost near zero.
Use round numbers ($2160 not $2,159.99) and remove commas ($2160 not $2,160) for psychological pricing effect.
Never lower prices. If budget is tight, keep price and remove deliverables instead.
Wage separation: pool revenue -> pay business expenses -> pay yourself fixed weekly salary -> keep remainder as business profit.
Only niche down after testing all 4 for 60 days. Generalists compete on price, specialists on expertise.
Physical partnerships (matted prints in coffee shops, lobbies, tourism spots with QR codes) outlast social media posts.
Most talented photographers don't make the most money. Systems are the moat, not talent.

weird_gold: Remove commas from prices as a psychological trick ($2160 looks smaller than $2,160) - counter-intuitive but effective.
The gallery upsell 48-hour expiration timer as scarcity/urgency lever: marginal cost zero, but time-pressure drives 30-40% attachment rate.
Physical prints in coffee shops/lobbies with QR codes as superior lead gen vs. paid social: persistent, zero-cost, outlasts algorithm changes.
Wage separation system (fixed weekly salary regardless of seasonal booking fluctuation) eliminates boom-bust decision paralysis and lets operator see true business profit.
Authority pivot as 3-legged moat: client work, teaching, digital products reinforce each other; removing any one leg weakens all three.
Spec work (shoot product, gift watermarked images, pitch retainer) eliminates client risk by showing finished work on real product instead of portfolio promises.
